hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated manganate(VII) does to a C=C bond, it splits the molecule completely at the double bond.

Recall how the product depends on how many alkyl groups are on each C of the C=C, a $\text{CH}_2=$ end gives $\text{CO}_2$, a $\text{RCH}=$ gives $\text{RCOOH}$, and a $\text{R}_2\text{C}=$ gives a ketone.
Look for the alkene that has one H on one side of the double bond and zero H on the other side, so you get one acid plus one ketone.
walkthrough:
**Recall the cleavage rule**

Hot, concentrated $\text{MnO}_4^- / \text{H}^+$ cleaves every $\text{C=C}$ into two carbonyl fragments.

$$\text{RCH}=\text{CHR}' \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{R}'\text{COOH}$$
$$\text{RCH}=\text{CR}'_2 \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{R}'_2\text{C}=\text{O}$$
$$\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{CR}'_2 \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{O} + \text{R}'_2\text{C}=\text{O}$$

**Translate the target into substitution**

We want one carboxylic acid plus one ketone.

That means one C of the double bond must be $\text{RCH}=$ with one H, and the other C must be $\text{R}_2\text{C}=$ with no H. This is a trisubstituted alkene of the type $\text{RCH}=\text{CR}_2$.

**Check each alkene**

A is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, terminal, gives $\text{CO}_2$ plus acid. B is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, disubstituted with one H each side, gives two acids. C is tetrasubstituted $\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{CR}_2$, gives two ketones.

Only D is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH(CH}_3\text{)}_2$, with zero H on the left C and one H on the right C, so it splits to propanone and 2-methylpropanoic acid.

options.A: A is pent-1-ene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The $\text{CH}_2=$ end is oxidised fully to $\text{CO}_2$ and water under hot concentrated conditions, while the other side gives butanoic acid. No ketone is formed.
options.B: B is pent-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Both carbons are $\text{RCH}=$, each with one H, so cleavage gives two carboxylic acids, ethanoic acid and propanoic acid. No ketone is formed.
options.C: C is tetrasubstituted, $\text{(CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{)(CH}_3\text{)C}=\text{C(CH}_3\text{)}_2$. Both carbons are $\text{R}_2\text{C}=$ with no vinylic H, so cleavage gives two ketones, butan-2-one and propanone. No carboxylic acid is formed.
options.D: D is 2,4-dimethylpent-2-ene, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH(CH}_3\text{)}_2$. The left $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C}=$ fragment with no H gives the ketone propanone, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C}=\text{O}$, and the right $\text{RCH}=$ fragment gives the carboxylic acid 2-methylpropanoic acid, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCOOH}$. This matches acid plus ketone exactly.
